title: DigRF v4-style baseband / RF IC serial link endpoint (8b/10b, framed logical channels)

fields.desc: K28.5 sync symbols at the start of a burst (0 = 1)
K28.5 fillers in a row before the lane stops (K29.7)

regs.name: CTL
regs.desc: Register access to the peer; writing CTL commits it. A read is answered through RSP (or RSP_TIMEOUT); the next access waits for it

regs.name: RSP
regs.desc: Read data from the peer; reading RSP frees it

regs.name: INT_TX
regs.desc: Interrupt message to the peer; writing INT_TX commits it

regs.name: INT_RX
regs.desc: Interrupt message from the peer; reading INT_RX frees it

fields.desc: the receiver is aligned to the incoming burst

irqs.name: RSP_TIMEOUT
irqs.desc: a read got no response within CFG.cfg_timeout

irqs.name: ERR_CODE
irqs.desc: 8b/10b code violation or disparity error (the receiver realigns)

irqs.name: ERR_FRAME
irqs.desc: bad header or size, unexpected control symbol, data between frames, or a response with no matching read

irqs.name: UNDERRUN
irqs.desc: a data payload byte was missing and sent as 0

notes: tx_p / rx_p are the lanes (one bit per PCLK, held at 0 while stopped).
reg_we / reg_re / reg_addr / reg_wdata / reg_rdata connect to the local register bank the peer accesses; reg_rdata is sampled one PCLK after reg_re.

dtx_* and drx_* connect to the local data path (IQ samples): dtx_valid offers a frame byte by byte, dtx_size / dtx_chan with its first byte; drx_* delivers received bytes without back-pressure, drx_abort ends a frame that broke off.
